root.name: Modern Defense: Beefeater Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 g6 2. c4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c5 4. d5 Bxc3+ 5. bxc3 f5

overview: Black trades the g7 bishop for the c3 knight and plays ...f5, giving White the bishop pair and a big pawn centre in exchange for control of e4 and the dark squares. White has doubled c-pawns but a space advantage, and the d5 pawn clamps the position. It is a rare, unbalanced line that Black plays for surprise.

white_ideas.idea: Use the bishop pair and the d5/c4 space
Play e3 and Nf3, then open the position with e4

black_ideas.idea: Control e4 and e5 with ...f5 and ...Nf6
Aim at the c3 weaknesses and the dark squares

typical_structures.structure: Doubled c-pawns for White, locked c4/d5 against ...c5/...d6

character.notes: Black gives up his fianchetto bishop and weakens his king; play is unbalanced.

gambit.notes: Only the bishop pair changes, no pawn is given.

soundness.notes: Black gives up the bishop pair and weakens e6; I think engines favour White.

structure.notes: The c4/d5 pawns lock the centre against ...c5.

level.notes: A risky surprise line, never a first repertoire choice.
